rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each listed source carries a freshness STAMP, not just a to-do.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM this rule prevents: source debt that never comes due before a cohort, and a citing file granting itself more runway than the owning file did. Both are present at L171. `[checked:2026-08-15 result:OK due:2027-02-15]` https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal. (a) §11a's unified-scope clause names this exact case — `a Claude Code capability claim is a source whose URL is the docs page and whose "open" is a live test — same stamp, due:cohort` — and this stamp uses a calendar date ~5 months PAST the cohort instead. (b) The DUE arithmetic is the one §11a bans by name: `Never checked+6mo`; 2026-08-15 + 6mo = 2027-02-15 exactly. (c) The sibling stamp for the identical URL, `lectures/the-agent-loop.md:92`, reads `[checked:2026-08-01 result:CAVEAT due:cohort]` — tighter date AND a CAVEAT result (`Opt-in, off by default`) that L171 does not carry; §11a permits divergence `only toward the tighter date`. Mechanically demonstrated: `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-09-15` printed `summary: 38 block · 74 warn · 80 info · 191 ok`, and grepping its full output for `run-the-first-experiment` returns only line 267 (`...run-the-first-experiment.md:172 [CAVEAT due:2026-08-09]`, INFO bucket). L171 is not in BLOCK, not in WARN, not in INFO — it cleared into the silent OK bucket, so a live-moving `/goal` capability ships to the 2026-09-15 room with no re-check scheduled.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Re-stamp L171 as a capability check: `due:cohort`, and carry the sibling's CAVEAT (opt-in, off by default) rather than a bare OK.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A green check must measure the fact, not a proxy that co-varies with it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM: an instrument whose pass is uninformative, so a real defect reads as clean. Present, twice, and I ran the instrument to show it. `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-09-15` files L172 — `[checked:2026-07-02 result:CAVEAT due:2026-08-09]` — under `INFO (80) — known/accepted:` with the note `└─ accepted caveat`. That due date passed 12 days ago (today 2026-08-21) and the cohort is 2026-09-15, yet the row is presented as accepted: the script routes on `result:` and never compares an expired `due` once a row is CAVEAT. Tell (b) from the rule is also live in the same run — the BLOCK count of 38 includes 3 rows from the script's OWN fixture (`curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.fixture.md:4,5,6`) and 8 rows from `curriculum/evals/instances/*.json`, i.e. quoted stamp text inside prior eval verdicts, not shipping surfaces.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Two separate items: re-check + re-stamp L172 before 2026-09-15; and (script-owner's call, not this file's) make CAVEAT rows compare `due` against `--target` and filter instances/fixtures out of the shipping count.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A word-presence claim needs an unprimed read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This rule fired on my own method and I obeyed it. My first fetch named both target strings verbatim in the prompt — a primed read, inadmissible for a presence claim — and it came back muddled, quoting one sentence as `surrounding` and then restating my own string back at me. I re-fetched cold (`how does this essay define (a) the bitter lesson and (b) the garbage can model ... quote the essay's own defining sentences verbatim`), naming neither string, and the page volunteered both unprompted: `encoding human understanding into an AI tends to be worse than just letting the AI figure out how to solve the problem, and adding enough computing power until it can do it better than any human` and `problems, solutions, and decision-makers are dumped in together, and decisions often happen when these elements collide randomly`. L175's two quotes are exact truncations of these, so the stamp survives an unprimed read.

The row is one line above a contract that already HAS the marker §6e asks for — L154's first row pins the branch + SHA into the protected `Run coordinates` block in `task.md`.
